newsitem.title: USA: US Apr spot natgas prices steady ahead of holiday.
newsitem.headline: US Apr spot natgas prices steady ahead of holiday.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices for April were little changed again Thursday, with some firmness evident in the western and Appalachian markets, industry sources said.
Swing April Louisiana Gulf prices were talked flat to one cent lower in the low-$1.80s per mmBtu, with Henry Hub quoted at $1.82-1.85.
For the remainder of March, Henry Hub prices held in the low-$1.90s, while in south Texas, most traders closed deals for the long weekend around $1.80.
In west Texas, where above-normal temperatures and storage injections continued, Permian prices for April 1 rose about two cents to the mid-$1.60s to about $1.70.
Another factor contributed to the price uptick was the extended outage at the 1,070 megawatt San Onofre 2 nuclear unit in California. The company now estimates the unit will restart on April 2.
Southern California border prices for next month were up about four cents to about $1.80.
For the remaining days of March, Permian and border prices were in the low-$1.70s and about $1.86, respectively.
At the New York city-gate, April prices remained at $2.17-2.20, while weekend prices were stagnant at $2.20.
In the Appalachian region, April prices moved about three cents higher to about $2.05-2.06 on Columbia and $2.10-2.13 on CNG.
Cooler temperatures are forecast for the Northeast this weekend, but plentiful storage supplies and the usual drop in demand over the long holiday weekend negated that demand.

American Gas Association said Wednesday stocks in the East Region were down 63 bcf to 406 bcf, but were still 189 bcf ahead of a year ago. Overall, storage inventories showed a decline of 54 bcf to 832 bcf, or 26 percent of capacity.
In the Midcontinent, April prices remained in the low-to-mid $1.70s, up about 10 cents from March indices. Swing prices were also steady to lower in the mid-$1.70s.
Chicago city-gate for next month was quoted a little higher at $1.96-2.00, while swing gas sold at $1.94-1.98.
Temperatures throughout the Midwest are forecast to remain above normal Friday but then return to near-normal this weekend.
